chapter: Arriving in New York: the Nest Club and Harlem nightlife
title: Night people proprietors in other cities and the segregated hotels
summary: Danny and Milt list Black club and hotel owners like the Montgomerys in Buffalo and the Cole Brothers, and the poor Black hotels musicians stayed in.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: But yeah, you had like Bill Bottoms, and the people up in Buffalo -- Ann Montgomery...
...and her husband. Yeah, they had two... They ran everything in Buffalo.
Yeah, they had a nightclub up there.
And the Cole Brothers. All them people was Night...
The Cole Brothers. That was in Cincinnati, wasn't it?

No. One of them was in Cincinnati and one was in Baltimore. There was a chain of them brothers. They was all hotel owners. And one had the... The Vendome in Buffalo, that was the Cole Brothers. And then I went through there with that little girl...

Yeah, we were stuck, Black guys; we were stuck. We had to stay in the hotels, because we couldn't stay in the White hotels. And they treated us like a dog. Wouldn't clean up the rooms or nothin', boy. They sure gave us... You remember those hotels we used to stay at in the South?

Yeah, sure. They didn't care nothin' about nobody, and (?)you'd pay them(?). But they had a group of musicians that would go through and ransack a hotel. They would do so many ungodly things. I mean...
